coordinates.note: Repo convention: x from bow (0) to aft, +Z is the shuttle-slot side, -Z the docking side. Azimuth theta is measured from +Y toward +Z: y = r cos(theta), z = r sin(theta). Under torch thrust aft is down.

torch.note: Torch working card from main (src/wayfarer_torch_mode_cards.py MODE_CARDS): mdot and ve per mode; thrust = mdot ve. The ship's heat rejection is sized for 11.361 TW of jet power, so modes whose card power is higher (FAST, HARD, LIMIT) are throttled in mass flow to that ceiling; the 4 g crew cap may throttle further.
torch.neutron_source_prov: ENGINEERING_ASSUMPTION (v0.5.2): pulsed shell burns at the burn point; 0.6 m of aim scatter along x and 0.3 m sideways

thrust_line_offset.prov: DERIVED: the whole torch chain (shield, reactor, nozzle, aft RCS) is offset sideways so its thrust line runs through the middle of the centre-of-mass range; build_v05.py picks the offset that minimises the worst trim angle over S1-S7
thrust_line_offset.rule: among protected-water splits and offsets whose worst trim over S1-S7 is within the design target (70% of the 0.5 deg limit), take the smallest offset; ENGINEERING_ASSUMPTION

torch.thrust_point_prov: KT_DECISION (2026-10-25, torch heat package step S4): each pellet burns 6 m aft of the reactor face (x 46.3), still inside the 53.3 m envelope; the thrust line pivots here

heat_package.prov: KT_DECISION 2026-10-25 (torch heat exploration; non-governing model in torch/)
what: Heat leaves with the exhaust: each fuel pellet is wrapped in a shell of remass that soaks up the burn and becomes the exhaust (pulsed torch, Fusion Driven Rocket principle)
Cleaner fuel: helium-3-rich, spin-polarised D-He3 (neutrons ~0.76% of fusion energy)
Thick, closed shell: traps 99.98% of the burn's light and 85% of its neutron energy
Burn 6 m aft of the reactor face
Four hot fins at 1,750 K aft of the shield, on the strake lines
heat_package.fusion_tw: about 12.6 TW for the 11.36 TW jet (DERIVED in the model)
heat_package.pulses: about 1-10 per second; 0.3-3 kt each at full power (DERIVED in the model)

mode_cards.prov: KT_DECISION 2026-10-26 (agree 1): main's working card governs; src/wayfarer_torch_mode_cards.py at main 19377b85

torch.jet_power_ceiling_prov: DERIVED: the hot fins (G4) and strake cryo span are sized at 11.361 TW (CRUISE card power); a higher ceiling needs larger fins

tvc.prov: KT_DECISION 2026-10-26 (agree 2): the magnetic nozzle steers the thrust line by up to 1 deg (asymmetric coil current), enough to hold the thrust line through the CG with trim plus an assumed 0.5 deg error (0.85 deg). ENGINEERING_ASSUMPTION: no qualified nozzle capability yet; declared in G10

tanks.kind: C-shaped wrap-around, four strake grooves (v0.4 CWRAP_G)

cells.note: Four isolatable cells: port/starboard split at the keel (theta 270) and the slot, fore/aft split at mid-length. Q7: one cell isolated = 25% of remass.

tanks.x_note: DERIVED: the solid model gives about 24.3 m2/m of section, and the tank's internal structure (tie-webs, baffles, slot walls, bulkheads) displaces about 6 m3; 13.5 m gives about 322 m3 net, 2% over the 315 m3 needed.

crown_dome.doctrine: open only at low speed or with the bow facing away from the dust flow (braking and tail-first coasting); closed for solar particle events, radiation belts, torch burns and Loom formation and translation. Stuck closed is safe; stuck open: turn the bow out of the dust flow.
crown_dome.views: 37 pane protective crown over transparent monolithic pressure dome; visual acceptance and human optics require review
crown_dome.displays: pilot displays on arms from the flight deck (they no longer hang from the nose)
crown_dome.mass_allocation_note: Physical ceramic inner dome mass is split across existing pressure_vessel shell 8g/cm2 mass PLUS incremental crown pane mass. Inner ceramic physical mass=4.345t, outer=1.407t; credit existing pressure shell~3.311t; delta from reserve only.

litter.prov: rigid litter 2.0 x 0.60 m (Sol's stretcher) with patient, 0.35 m deep

casualty_doctrine: Casualty moves happen at 0 g: the captain orders coast, which is available at any time (an emergency burn means everyone is already in a couch).
The litter is carried with its length along the ship's axis: through 2.05 m doors, end-first down the port ladder shaft (theta 180), out of the shaft at L4 and straight through the medical opening.
Under thrust the casualty stays in their couch or berth (each is a 5 g couch) and is treated there until coast.
Above ~1.5 g everyone is in a couch; no casualty moves.

ladder_shafts.rungs_on: inboard face (r 1.0 m side), so the outboard side of the shaft stays clear for a litter

l4_l5_isolation.prov: CLAUDE_DESIGN v0.5.6: floor L4 becomes a pressure bulkhead so a depressurised L5 (airlock, docking tunnel) cannot take the rest of the habitat. Two hinged pressure hatches (rounded-square, ISS CBM-hatch style) close the ladderways; a pressure plug with a lift hatch and feedthroughs seals the trunk at the same plane. Hatches stand open in normal operations and close automatically on a pressure drop

shelter_backup.prov: Consumption: Barta, Anderson and Lange, NASA JSC 2015 (ntrs.nasa.gov 20150009498): O2 0.84, CO2 1.00, drinking water 1.62, food 0.62 kg per person per day. Stored backup on L4 for 72 h if the life-support room's regenerative systems are unavailable; drinking water drawn from the shelter's own water jacket. Battery covers 24 h of essential loads; the plant otherwise powers the shelter

accel_doctrine.cap_evidence: NASA OCHMO acceleration brief: +Gx 4 g tolerable up to at least 60 min; 2 g at least 24 h
accel_doctrine.prov: CLAUDE_DESIGN v0.5.6: crew doctrine caps sustained thrust at 4 g (the 5 g structural rating stays as margin, emergencies only). [V2 6113] limits time on the back with feet raised to 3 h 15 min (nominal 2 h 45 min); burns longer than 2 h 45 min are split by a 30 min coast break

viewport_band.prov: CLAUDE_DESIGN v0.5.7 rev 3 (kT: 'maximize viewports'): a continuous panoramic band round the L2 common deck at standing and seated eye height, taller (1.6 m) in the observation lounge; skips the washroom (270-300 deg). NON-GOVERNING; SOL TO AGREE; rev 4 (kT 2026-10-26, after Sol's review of the rev 3.1 study): titanium edge rings, a mid transom in the lounge, plate-sized panes on the crown's 2226 ceramic milestone
viewport_band.mullions: Osteon titanium mullions every 15 deg (1.13 m), forking into the sill and head beams; they carry the deck's axial load (5 g x 1.5 of everything ahead, plus the pressure end load) across the band
viewport_band.panes: flat plates between frame members (the glass is not trusted to pass hoop tension through its edges); two pressure panes each carrying full load, plus 8 mm debris and 3 mm scratch panes; flaw-controlled 2226 ceramic (the crown dome's milestone): 16 mm in the 0.6 m band, 18 mm in the lounge
viewport_band.shutter: Strata tambour band: slats run round the hull in a track and stow in the head beam; closed flush with the armour at cruise speed, in solar storms and in burns, and for night
viewport_band.heat: low-e inner coating (emissivity 0.1): ~42 W per m2 of glazing radiated to space with the shutters open

edge_rings.note: sill and head rings, all the way round (they close over the washroom); carry the hoop across the band and act as continuous beams between mullions (habitat/viewport_band_study.py)

attachments.kind: titanium flexure fingers between ring and shell (Osteon detail), stiff along the ship, compliant radially
attachments.prov: REV 5 (structure review C): Ti expands ~17x more than the CFRP laminate; over a 50 K shutter cycle the ring grows ~1.7 mm more in radius than the shell (11 mm round the circumference). The fingers take that as bending instead of fighting it through bolts.

lounge_transom.note: mid-height Osteon transom across the 1.6 m lounge panes, halving their span

viewport_band.mullion_roots: 4 x M16 Ti bolts in double shear per root (or an integral Osteon fork)

longerons.prov: CLAUDE_DESIGN v0.5.7 (structure/longeron_study.py, kT 2026-10-25 'consolidate'): four CFRP tubes in an X, matching canon's 4 axial longerons. The upper pair stay where the v0.5.6 slot sills were (edging the bay slot); the lower pair mirror them in the tank's lower cells. Sized at 5 g x 1.5 to a 250 MPa design stress (400 MPa floor x 0.62 for impact, joints, environment). v0.5.6 had 3 planks + 2 sills (36.9 t) running at 65 MPa. NON-GOVERNING; SOL TO REVIEW REV 5 (structure review 2026-10-26): wall 72 -> 84 mm (area 0.0830 m2, 1% margin) so axial + bending (thrust-line offset 13.5 MN m + 0.5 deg thrust error 9.1 MN m) stays within the 250 MPa design stress

tank_structure.prov: ENGINEERING_ASSUMPTION (structural concept). Plate bending: Navier series for simply supported plates (Timoshenko and Woinowsky-Krieger, Theory of Plates and Shells), matching Roark Table 11.4 case 1a to 3 decimals; nu 0.3
tank_structure.concept: Radial tie-webs join the inner and outer walls so the C-shaped cell does not try to open under pressure; perforated ring baffles every 1 m also stop slosh; the flat slot walls are supported by the inner corner, the sill longeron and the outer corner; solid bulkheads at both ends and mid-length; a solid radial wall at the keel separates port and starboard cells.
